key_insight: A geometrically-exact planar beam formulation can incorporate hyperelasticity consistently by separating in-plane kinematics from out-of-plane constitutive reduction, with plane stress giving robust response while plane strain amplifies Poisson-ratio sensitivity.
engineering_relevance: This provides a practical finite-element framework for modeling slender structures with nonlinear geometry and nonlinear materials without forcing cross-sectional and constitutive assumptions to be coupled.
method: Start from a conventional three-field geometrically-exact planar beam with full geometric nonlinearity.
Enrich the kinematics with a global field that allows in-plane thickness deformation.
Treat the out-of-plane response separately via plane-stress or plane-strain constitutive reduction for Saint Venant-Kirchhoff and Neo-Hookean laws.
evidence_signal: Benchmark comparisons in the abstract show near-identical centerline deformations under plane stress across Poisson ratios, while plane strain produces noticeable stiffening at higher Poisson ratios; hyperelastic models agree globally with differences mainly in local out-of-plane stretch.
watch_item: Plane-strain reduction can strongly over-stiffen the beam at high Poisson’s ratio, so the constitutive reduction must be chosen carefully for the intended physical setting.
paper_title: On finite elements for geometrically-exact planar beams with hyperelastic material models
